overview.mechanism: Ketoanalogues are nitrogen-free precursors of corresponding amino acids; these preparations are studied as part of supervised protein-restricted nutrition, rather than as independent kidney-protective tablets.
uses: Adjunct to a prescribed protein-restricted nutrition plan in selected patients with CKD; exact formulations differ.

paragraphs.text: A 2024 meta-analysis of 16 trials found possible kidney and biochemical benefits with ketoanalogues plus protein restriction, but no significant mortality difference; larger trials remain necessary.

A pragmatic randomized trial found no additional benefit of the supplemented very-low-protein strategy under regular nephrology care. Results depend on the complete nutrition intervention and cannot be attributed to tablets alone.

These registry headings do not establish that all brands contain identical amino acids, calcium salts or strengths. Check the individual formulation before calculating tablets or calcium exposure; similarly named pages must not be merged on wording alone.

KDIGO 2024 allows consideration of a supplemented very-low-protein diet in adults at risk of kidney failure who are willing and able to follow it, under close supervision. This is a complete dietary intervention, not an instruction to add tablets to an unrestricted diet.

Do not prescribe low- or very-low-protein diets in metabolically unstable CKD. Protein restriction in children risks impaired growth; older adults with frailty or sarcopenia may need higher protein and calorie targets. These cautions concern the diet and cannot be solved by supplementation alone.
